# One message per frame, even under a burst

A frame never carries two message bodies. Substitution from a message body in a
node reacting to that message is always well-defined, in either queue mode.

## The template

```yaml
name: one-message-per-frame-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: ops/step
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        label: {type: string}
      required: [label]
nodes:
  - type: reactor
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/step
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          label:
            type: string
            source: "{{messages.ops/step.label}}"
```

## Back the queue up

Hold the first frame open with a pause-mode `before_dispatch` breakpoint, then
send three distinctly-labelled messages so the queue genuinely backs up:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/breakpoints" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"matcher":{"node_type":"reactor"},"checkpoint":"before_dispatch","mode":"pause"}'

for label in first second third; do
  curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: step-$label" \
    -d "{\"type\":\"ops/step\",\"payload\":{\"label\":\"$label\"}}"
done
```

Resume every hit until the queue drains, then read back:

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/frames"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

## In backlog mode

All three messages are delivered across three frames. Each delivered message
names a distinct frame, and each frame's triggering message is one of the three.

The reacting node settles three times, resolving one label per run in arrival
order — `first`, `second`, `third` — and no run records a
`template_resolution_failed`.

Every frame the burst opened names the one declared message type.

## In coalescing mode

Create the instance with `"message_queue_mode":"coalesce"` and run the same
burst. Two messages survive, delivered across two frames — still one message per
frame — and the node resolves one label per run.

This is the mode where merging two bodies into one frame would be most
plausible, and it does not happen. No template has to refuse a coalesced frame
at run time.
